chunks: Ali ibn al-Hasan ibn Fadhl from al-Abbas ibn Amir from Dawud ibn al-Husayn from Mansur ibn Hazim said:

I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): A man married a woman and specified a dowry for her, then he died leaving her, without having entered into her. He said: 'She has the full dowry and she has the inheritance.' I said: 'Indeed, they narrated from you that she has half the dowry.' He said: 'They do not preserve accurately from me; that is only for the divorced woman.'

Although if she were safe from that, it would be permissible for us to interpret it as being preferable for the woman, if her husband dies leaving her, or for her guardians if she dies, that they leave half the dowry as preferable rather than obligatory.
And no one can say to us: Why did you say that by saying: It is obligatory upon the man or upon his heirs to give her half the dowry, and it is preferable for them to give her the other half.

Because our narrations have been supported by the apparent meaning of the Quran, so it is not permissible for us to turn away from its apparent meaning except with evidence, and these narrations are not like that, but they are independent of the Quran.
And if they were like that, it would be permissible for us to turn in them from obligation to preference.
Although what I choose and issue a fatwa on is that I say: If the man dies leaving his wife before entering into her, she has the entire dowry, and if she dies, her guardians have half the dowry.

I made this distinction because all the narrations we presented regarding the obligation of the entire dowry, for they include if the man dies, and there is nothing in them that if she dies, her guardians have the full dowry.

So I do not exceed the narrations, and as for what opposed them from the narrations regarding equalizing between the death of each of them in the obligation of half the dowry, it is interpreted as preference which we presented.
And as for the narrations that include that if she dies, her guardians have half the dowry, they are interpreted on their apparent meaning and I do not need to interpret them.
And this opinion is safer for interpreting the narrations, and God is the Giver of success to the right.

And whenever the man divorces his wife, then he dies leaving her, if it is a divorce with which he has the right of return, she must observe the waiting period of the longer of the two periods, the waiting period of the one whose husband died leaving her.
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on the dowry if the husband dies before consummating the marriage according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) establishes that upon the husband's death before consummation, the wife is entitled to the full dowry and inheritance, distinguishing this from the half-dowry rule applicable to divorce. He employs a sophisticated hermeneutic strategy, interpreting conflicting narrations by assigning the 'half' reports to voluntary charity (istihbab) rather than obligation, thereby preserving the apparent meaning (zahir) of the 'full' reports. This ruling underscores the Shia principle of adhering to the explicit text of hadith unless a clear counter-evidence necessitates reinterpretation, ensuring legal consistency with the Quranic framework.
